title: UsageRecorded
description: common.usage-recorded@1 (roadmap WS-N task 4, ADR-014): one rollup of a developer project's use of one capability in one environment over one closed window (an hour or a day), as the service that owns the capability counted it. The payload of every <service>.usage.recorded event; OpenVibe.Network adds them up per project and day for the project's dashboard on OpenVibe.Codes. The producer counts in the transaction that does its own accounting (a job's end, a stored event, a delivery attempt) and writes the rollup to its outbox after the window has closed: never one event per request. Totals, not deltas: a later event with the same key (source, project_id, env, capability, dimension, unit, window_start) replaces the earlier one, and a lower revision never replaces a higher one. Envelope: subject { type: project, id: <project_id> }, visibility internal, priority low, actor the producing service. Never carries a subject id, an address, a session, a request's input or content, or a file name.

project_id.description: The developer project whose app token did the work.

env.description: The environment of that app token.

capability.description: The capability the usage counts against: tools.job.create, tools.tool.run, events.app.publish, events.app.subscribe.

dimension.description: Optional finer key inside the capability, as the producer names it: a job type (img.process) or a tool id (image-resize). Never the id of a person, an app, a request or a job.

unit.description: What quantity counts (jobs, events, deliveries, requests, bytes, tokens): the same word a Network project quota uses for its unit.

window_start.description: UTC, on the hour (midnight for a day).

quantity.description: Units used in the window, by work that succeeded and work that failed alike.

errors.description: Operations in the window that failed or were refused: a job that failed, a publish refused with a problem, a webhook attempt without a 2xx. A refused operation may use no unit, so errors can exceed quantity.

error_codes.description: The errors by problem code (at most 20 codes; the rest are only in errors).

samples.description: The last failures of the window, newest first, so a developer can find them in their own logs.

status.description: The HTTP status the failure was answered with, when there was one.

trace_id.description: The W3C trace id of the request (or event) that failed.

ref.description: What failed, when the project can look it up with its own token: a job, an event, an AI run, a Media object. Never a subject.

revision.description: 1 when absent. A producer that re-emits a window with corrected totals raises it.
